pages.text: Faisal and his grandfather drove to a quiet beach by the Red Sea. They put up their tent near the soft sand. "Tonight, we will sleep under the stars," Grandfather said with a smile.
After dinner, Faisal walked along the beach with a torch. Suddenly, something moved near his foot. It was a tiny turtle, smaller than his hand! Then he saw another one, and another.

But the baby turtles were walking away from the sea, towards the bright lights of a small café. "Why are they going the wrong way?" Faisal asked. "Baby turtles follow the brightest light," Grandfather explained. "It is usually the moon on the water."
"The café is brighter than the moon!" Faisal said. "We must help them." He switched off his torch, and Grandfather turned off the car lights. But the café lights were still shining.

Faisal ran to the café as fast as he could. "Excuse me, sir," he said to the owner. "Can you please turn off your lights for a few minutes? Baby turtles are lost on the beach." The man looked surprised, but he quickly pressed a switch.
Now the beach was dark, and the silver moon shone on the sea. Slowly, the little turtles turned around. One by one, they crawled down to the waves and swam away. Faisal counted twenty-three turtles!

The next morning, Faisal and the café owner made a sign: "Turtle Beach – Please keep lights off at night." "One day, those turtles will come back here to lay their eggs," Grandfather said. Faisal looked at the blue sea and felt very proud.

options: To a farm in the mountains
To a quiet beach by the Red Sea
To a big city with many lights

pages.text: Yousef wanted to win the school food fair. "What can we cook, Grandma?" he asked. Grandma smiled. "We're going to make kleeja, my special date cookies."
In the kitchen, they mixed flour, butter and cardamom. The house smelled wonderful. Then Grandma's phone rang, and she went to the living room. "Don't touch anything!" she called.
But little Huda wanted to help. She took a white jar and put three big spoons into the bowl. "More sugar makes it sweeter!" she said happily. Nobody saw the label on the jar. It said SALT.
Later, Yousef tasted the dough. "Yuck! It's so salty!" he shouted. Huda started to cry. The fair was tomorrow, and there were no more dates in the house.

Grandma looked at the bowl and laughed. "Don't worry. A good cook can fix a mistake," she said. She took cheese from the fridge and za'atar from the cupboard. "Today, our kleeja is going to be different."

The next day, the tables at the fair were full of cakes, chocolate and biscuits. The judges tried them all. "Too much sugar!" one judge whispered. Then she bit into Yousef's warm cheese cookie, and her eyes opened wide.
Yousef won the prize for the Most Surprising Dish! Everyone wanted the recipe. "It was a team idea," Yousef said, and he gave the prize to Huda. "She's our secret chef!"

stories.title: The Night the Lights Went Out

pages.text: Lina loved sounds. She heard music everywhere: in the bubbling coffee pot, in the rain on the window, and in her little brother's spoon on his plate. She kept a notebook and wrote down all her favourite sounds.

One morning, Ms Huda said, "Our class is going to play music for our families next Thursday!" Everyone was excited, but Lina was worried. "I can't play the keyboard or the drum," she said quietly. "Then you can help me with the lights," Ms Huda said with a smile.

On Thursday evening, the school hall was full of mothers, fathers and grandparents. Hamad started the first song on the electric keyboard, and the music was loud and bright. Suddenly, there was a strange noise, and all the lights went out.
The hall was dark and very quiet. The keyboard was silent too, because there was no electricity. A baby started to cry, and Hamad whispered, "What are we going to do now?"
Lina remembered her notebook of sounds. She turned on the torch on Ms Huda's phone and tapped two pencils on a table: tap, tap, tap-tap-tap. "Everyone, copy me!" she called.

First the children clapped, and then the parents joined in. Some people tapped their feet, and some knocked gently on their chairs. Soon the whole dark hall was full of music, and the baby stopped crying and laughed.

When the lights came back ten minutes later, everyone cheered. The next day, Ms Huda gave Lina a real drum. "You don't need electricity to make music," she said. "You only need good ears and a brave heart."

She couldn't play the keyboard or the drum

In the story, "whispered" means:

Because Lina showed she was a real musician

stories.title: The Case of the Missing Dates

pages.text: Layla wanted to be a detective. She always carried a small notebook and a magnifying glass in her bag. One morning, Grandma came into the kitchen with an empty plate. "My dates are gone again!" she said.

Every evening, Grandma put a plate of fresh dates on the table in the garden for her guests. But every morning, some of the dates were missing. "Who is taking them?" asked Omar, Layla's little brother. "Let's find out," Layla said, and she opened her notebook.

First, Layla looked for clues. Under the table, she found four date stones and some tiny footprints in the sand. "These aren't Omar's footprints," she said. "They are too small, and they only have three thin toes!"
Omar laughed. "Maybe it's a very small thief with no shoes!" But Layla was thinking hard. Then she found a black and brown feather on the garden wall.
The next day, Layla and Omar woke up before sunrise. They hid behind the kitchen window and watched the table quietly. Soon they heard a loud, happy noise above the garden.

Two brown birds with yellow eyes flew down to the table. Each bird took a date and flew up to the top of the palm tree. Layla looked through her magnifying glass and saw a nest with three hungry baby birds inside!

"Case closed!" Layla said proudly at breakfast. Grandma smiled and put a small plate of dates near the palm tree for the birds. Then she covered the guests' dates with a net. "Now everyone in this garden can enjoy a good breakfast," she said.

options: A notebook and a magnifying glass

options: On the table in the garden

options: Things that help you find an answer

options: They had three thin toes, so they were not from a person

options: They wanted to hide them from Grandma
They were feeding their baby birds
They wanted to play with Omar

pages.text: Yousef loved superheroes. Every night, he drew comics about Captain Falcon, a hero who could fly faster than a plane. "I wish I had a superpower," he told his grandfather. Grandpa smiled and said, "Maybe you already have one."

On Friday evening, the family went to the old market. It was full of people, bright lights and the smell of spices. Yousef looked at everything carefully, like he always did before he drew something. He saw a small boy in a red cap. The boy was holding a toy camel and walking next to a woman with a green bag.

Later, near the perfume shop, Yousef heard someone crying. It was the boy in the red cap, but now he was alone. "I can't find my mum!" he cried. Yousef's heart was beating fast, but he knelt down and said, "Don't worry. I'll help you."

Yousef closed his eyes and remembered. Before, the boy's mother was buying dates at the shop next to the fountain. Her bag was green with yellow flowers on it. "Grandpa, follow me!" Yousef said, and they walked quickly through the busy market.
At the date shop, a woman was looking around. She looked very worried. In her hand, she held a green bag with yellow flowers. "Mama!" shouted the boy, and he ran into her arms.
The mother thanked Yousef again and again. "You are a real hero," she said. Yousef looked down at his shoes. "But I can't fly, and I don't have a cape."

Grandpa put his hand on Yousef's shoulder. "You noticed small things, and you were brave and kind. That is your superpower." That night, Yousef started a new comic. His new hero was called Captain Eyes.

options: He remembered small things he saw before

options: afraid that something bad will happen

options: Because his superpower was noticing things

stories.title: The Shoe Thief of the Desert

pages.text: Every winter, Faisal's family went camping in the desert. This year, Grandpa came too. They drove for two hours until they could see only red sand and a big blue sky.

Dad and Faisal put up the tent, and Noura helped Mum with the fire. At night, Grandpa pointed at the sky. "Look, that bright star always shows the north," he said. "Our grandfathers used the stars like a map."
Later, everyone was sleeping when Faisal heard a strange noise outside. Scratch, scratch, scratch! He looked out quietly, but he couldn't see anything in the dark.
In the morning, one of his shoes was missing! "Who took my shoe?" Faisal shouted. Grandpa laughed and pointed at the small footprints next to the tent. "The desert can tell you," he said.
Faisal and Noura followed the footprints with Grandpa. They walked past dry bushes and over a small hill. Faisal had to wear his sandals, and the sand was getting hotter and hotter.

Behind a big rock, they found a hole. Next to it was Faisal's shoe, and two baby foxes were playing with it! Their mother watched them with her big ears. "Shh," whispered Grandpa. "Don't go closer. This is their home."

They waited quietly, and soon the foxes ran back into their hole. Faisal picked up his shoe slowly. It had a few small holes now, but he didn't mind. "Now you can read the desert too," Grandpa said with a smile.

options: Because Faisal found a book in the sand

pages.text: The big clock above our school door was very old. Every morning, it rang at seven o'clock, and every student ran to class. But one Sunday, it stopped. Nobody knew why.
"Sports Day is on Thursday," said our teacher, Mr. Khalid. "We need the clock to start the races!" The headteacher called a repair man, but he was busy until next month.
In our class there was a new boy called Omar. He was very quiet, and he always sat alone at break time. That day, I saw him looking up at the clock for a long time.
"My grandfather mends clocks," Omar said softly. "I help him in his shop every weekend." I was surprised. "Can you fix our clock?" I asked, and he answered, "Maybe, but I need to see inside it."

Mr. Khalid brought a ladder, and Omar climbed up carefully. He opened the back of the clock and looked inside with a small torch. "There's a bird's nest in here!" he laughed. "It's stopping the wheels."
Omar moved the nest gently into a tree, and he cleaned the wheels with a soft brush. Then he turned a tiny key. Tick, tock, tick, tock! All the students in the yard cheered.
On Thursday, the clock rang, and the first race began. Omar ran in it, and I ran next to him. We didn't win, but we laughed all the way to the finish line. Now Omar never sits alone at break time.

options: He helps his grandfather in his shop

options: He made a friend and was not lonely anymore

He moved to a new school

stories.title: The Night the Lights Went Out

pages.text: It was a hot summer evening in Riyadh. Omar was playing a game on his tablet, Dad was watching football, and Mum was talking to Aunt Noura on the phone. Grandpa Saleh sat quietly in his chair with his coffee, and nobody was talking to him.
Suddenly, all the lights went out. The TV stopped, and the air conditioner was silent. "A power cut!" shouted Huda, Omar's little sister. "It's so dark!"
"It's too hot inside," said Dad. "Let's go up to the roof." They took a torch, some cold water and a plate of dates, and they climbed the stairs together.

On the roof, they heard a strange noise behind the water tank. Huda held Mum's hand tightly, and Omar was scared too. But he walked slowly towards the sound with the torch. Two shining green eyes looked back at him. It was only a small, thin cat!

Everyone laughed, and Huda gave the cat some water. Then Grandpa pointed at the sky. "Without the city lights, you can see the stars," he said. "When I was a boy in the desert, my father used these stars to find the way home."

Omar's tablet battery was empty, but he didn't care. He listened to Grandpa's stories about camels, long journeys and cold desert nights. Mum and Dad asked lots of questions, and Grandpa looked happier than ever.

After two hours, the lights came on again, but nobody wanted to go inside. "Grandpa," said Omar, "can we come up here every Thursday night?" Grandpa put his arm around him and smiled. "That's the best idea I've heard all year," he said.

options: He wanted to play games on his tablet there

He wanted to feed the cat every week

pages.text: Omar got a small drone for his tenth birthday. It had a camera, and he could see its pictures on his tablet. "Be careful with it," said his father. "It isn't a toy."
On Friday, the family visited Grandpa's farm in the desert. Grandpa looked worried. "My falcon, Saqr, flew away this morning and didn't come back," he said.
Omar had an idea. "My drone can fly high and look for him!" he said. Grandpa laughed. "A machine can find a bird? Well, let's try."
The drone flew over the palm trees and the sand hills. Omar and his cousin Lama watched the screen carefully. Suddenly Lama shouted, "Stop! What's that brown shape near the old well?"
Omar moved the camera closer. It was Saqr! The falcon was sitting on the ground, and a long string was caught around his leg. He couldn't fly.
The family drove to the well quickly. Grandpa spoke softly to the bird and cut the string with his small knife. Saqr opened his wings and climbed onto Grandpa's arm.
That evening, everyone drank tea and ate dates outside under the stars. "I was wrong about your drone," Grandpa said with a smile. "Next time, can you teach me how to fly it?"

pages.text: This story happened in Cairo, about one thousand years ago. A boy called Yusuf lived near the busy market. Every afternoon, he carried bread and dates to an old scholar called Ibn al-Haytham.
The scholar's room was always dark. "Why do you close the windows, sir?" Yusuf asked. "Because I am studying light," the scholar answered with a smile.
One day, Ibn al-Haytham made a tiny hole in the wooden window. A thin line of sunlight came into the room. Suddenly, Yusuf saw colours on the white wall opposite.
"Look! It's the street!" Yusuf shouted. He could see a camel, a man with a basket and the green palm trees. But everything was upside down!
"Light travels in straight lines," the scholar explained. "It comes from the camel, goes through the hole and arrives on the wall. Our eyes work in the same way." Yusuf's mouth was wide open.
At that time, many people believed that light came out of our eyes. Ibn al-Haytham wanted to prove the truth, so he tested his ideas again and again. Then he wrote everything in a big book.
Yusuf never forgot that afternoon, and when he grew up, he became a scholar too. Today, cameras still use Ibn al-Haytham's simple idea: a small hole and a dark room.

options: Light came from the moon only.

pages.text: Every spring, Faisal visited his grandfather's farm in the desert. On Friday morning, the sky was clear and blue, and the sun was hot. Faisal looked at his phone. "The weather app says it will be sunny all day, Grandpa!"
Grandpa stood still and looked up at the sky for a long time. "The birds are flying low, and the wind smells of dust," he said quietly. "A sandstorm is coming this afternoon."

Faisal laughed. "But my phone is very clever, Grandpa!" Grandpa smiled. "Your phone is clever, but the sky is older." An hour later, Faisal saw something strange: a tall brown wall was moving across the desert towards them.
"Quick! Help me with the goats!" Grandpa shouted. Faisal ran after the goats and pushed them into the barn. Then he closed all the windows in the house while the wind got louder and louder.

Outside, everything was brown and dark, and they couldn't see the palm trees. Inside, Grandpa made sweet tea, and they listened to the wind. "My father learned about the weather from the clouds and the stars," Grandpa said. "He didn't need an app."

After two hours, the wind stopped. Then Faisal heard a soft sound on the roof. Rain! He ran outside and held out his hands, and the cool drops fell on his face. "Rain in the desert!" he shouted happily.

A week later, tiny green plants and yellow flowers covered the sand. Faisal opened his notebook and wrote: "Grandpa's weather rules: watch the birds, smell the wind, and look at the sky." Then he smiled at Grandpa. "Now I have two weather forecasts, and the best one isn't on my phone!"

options: Phones are always right about the weather.

He can learn a lot about the weather from nature and from Grandpa.

grammar.title: Comparatives with -er than
grammar.ar: نستخدم صيغة المقارنة لنقارن بين شخصين أو شيئين. مع الصفات القصيرة نضيف -er إلى الصفة ثم نضع كلمة than، مثل: old ← older than. إذا انتهت الصفة بحرف e نضيف r فقط مثل nice ← nicer، وإذا انتهت بـ y نحذفها ونضيف ier مثل funny ← funnier. انتبه: لا نقول more older، بل older فقط.
examples: My brother is older than me.
My grandma is shorter than my grandpa.
My little sister is funnier than my cousin.

grammar.title: Adverbs of frequency: always, usually, sometimes, never
grammar.ar: ظروف التكرار تخبرنا كم مرة نفعل شيئًا: always (دائمًا)، usually (عادةً)، sometimes (أحيانًا)، never (أبدًا). نضعها قبل الفعل الأساسي، مثل: We usually play. لكن نضعها بعد فعل be، مثل: She is always kind. وفي العربية قد نضعها في أماكن مختلفة، أما في الإنجليزية فمكانها ثابت.
examples: We usually play football together.
She is always happy to help me.
We never fight about games.

words.ex: I wake up at half past six.
I get dressed and then I brush my hair.
I have breakfast with my family at seven o'clock.
I catch the bus to school at quarter past seven.
After lunch, I do my homework.
I go to bed at nine o'clock.

dialogue.t: What time do you wake up on school days?
I wake up at half past six.
What do you do next?
First I wash my face, then I have breakfast at seven o'clock.
And after that?
After that, I get dressed and catch the bus at quarter past seven.
What do you do in the evening?
I do my homework, then I read a story. Finally, I go to bed at nine o'clock.

grammar.title: Sequencing words and telling the time
grammar.ar: نستخدم كلمات الترتيب لنحكي الأحداث بالتسلسل: First (أولًا)، then (ثم)، after that (بعد ذلك)، finally (أخيرًا). ونستخدم حرف at قبل الوقت، مثل: at seven o'clock. ونستعمل المضارع البسيط للعادات اليومية، ومع he وshe نضيف s للفعل، مثل: He wakes up.
examples: First I wake up, then I brush my teeth.
I have lunch at one o'clock.
After that, my sister watches TV, and finally she goes to bed.

words.ex: My favourite colour is green.
I collect stickers of football players.
This game is really exciting.
Books about animals are interesting.
I like sports, for example, swimming and tennis.
Pizza is the best food in the world!

dialogue.t: What's your favourite hobby?
My favourite hobby is reading because I can learn new things.
What kind of books do you like?
I like adventure books. For example, I love stories about pirates and treasure.
Cool! What's your favourite food?
My favourite food is my mum's chicken with rice because it's delicious.
Mmm, that sounds good! Do you collect anything?
Yes, I collect stickers. I've got more than two hundred!

grammar.title: Giving reasons and examples: because / for example
grammar.ar: نستخدم because (لأنّ) لنشرح سبب حبّنا لشيء، وبعدها نكتب جملة كاملة فيها فاعل وفعل، مثل: because it is fun. ونستخدم For example (على سبيل المثال) لنعطي مثالًا يوضّح كلامنا. انتبه: في الإنجليزية نقول because it is fun وليس because fun، فلا تحذف الفاعل والفعل.
examples: My favourite sport is football because it is exciting.
I love animals. For example, I like cats, horses and dolphins.
My favourite subject is science because the experiments are interesting.

words.ex: My bed is next to the window.
The lamp is between the bed and the desk.
The bathroom is opposite my bedroom.
There are lots of books on the shelf.
My clothes are in the wardrobe.
My bedroom is upstairs.

dialogue.t: Do you live in a house or a flat?
I live in a flat on the fourth floor. It has three bedrooms.
Tell me about your room.
There is a big bed next to the window. There are two posters on the wall.
Have you got a desk?
Yes, there is a desk between my bed and the wardrobe. I do my homework there.
Do you share your room?
No, I don't. My brother's room is opposite my room.

grammar.title: There is / There are + prepositions of place
grammar.ar: نستخدم There is مع الاسم المفرد، وThere are مع الاسم الجمع، للتعبير عن وجود شيء في مكان ما (يوجد / توجد). ونستخدم حروف المكان مثل next to (بجانب) وbetween (بين) وon (على) وunder (تحت) لنقول أين يوجد الشيء. انتبه: لا نقول There is two chairs، بل There are two chairs.
examples: There is a lamp next to my bed.
There are three books on the shelf.
There is a rug between the bed and the desk.

words.ex: This watch is special to me.
My uncle gave me a present for my birthday.
I got this book from my grandma.
This box is made of wood.
I keep my shells in a small box.
This photo reminds me of our holiday.

dialogue.t: What have you brought today?
This is my toy camel. Its name is Sandy.
It's lovely! Where did you get it?
I got it from my grandpa. He gave it to me when I was six.
Why is it special to you?
I love it because it reminds me of my grandpa and his farm.
Where do you keep it?
I keep it on the shelf next to my bed.

grammar.title: Past simple irregular verbs: got, gave, bought
grammar.ar: نستخدم الماضي البسيط لنتحدّث عن أحداث انتهت في الماضي. بعض الأفعال شاذّة ولا نضيف لها ed، بل تتغيّر صيغتها تمامًا، مثل: get ← got، give ← gave، buy ← bought. وفي السؤال نستخدم did مع الفعل في صيغته الأصلية، مثل: Where did you get it? وليس Where did you got it?
examples: I got this ball from my dad.
My aunt gave me this bracelet last year.
We bought this kite at the beach.

words.ex: Last Friday I went to the park with my brother.
We played football in the afternoon.
On Saturday we visited my cousins.
I watched a film with my family at night.
We had lunch at my grandmother's house.
We played games all day. It was fun!

dialogue.t: Hi Omar! What did you do last weekend?
Last Friday I went to the beach with my family.
Cool! What did you do there?
We played football on the sand and we swam in the sea.
Was it hot?
Yes, it was very hot, but it was fun! What about you?
I visited my cousins. We watched a film and had pizza.
That sounds great!

grammar.title: Past Simple: regular and irregular verbs
grammar.ar: نستخدم الماضي البسيط للحديث عن أشياء حدثت وانتهت في الماضي، مثل عطلة نهاية الأسبوع الماضية. الأفعال المنتظمة نضيف لها ed مثل play ← played و visit ← visited. أما الأفعال غير المنتظمة فلها شكل خاص يجب حفظه مثل go ← went و have ← had و is ← was.
examples: Last Friday I went to the zoo.
We played basketball after lunch.
It was a great weekend.

words.ex: The desert was big and very quiet.
We drove to the desert in my dad's car.
I climbed the sand dunes with my sister.
I saw a big brown camel near our tent.
We slept in a tent under the stars.
I felt excited because it was my first trip to the desert.

dialogue.t: Where did you go on your holiday?
We drove to the desert. It took two hours.
Wow! What did you see?
I saw camels and huge sand dunes. At night I saw lots of stars.
How did you feel?
I felt excited because we slept in a tent!
Were you scared at night?
A little, but my dad told us funny stories, so I felt happy.

grammar.title: Talking about feelings: I felt ... because ...
grammar.ar: نستخدم I felt (شعرتُ) مع صفة لنصف مشاعرنا في الماضي، مثل I felt happy أو I felt tired. بعد ذلك نستخدم because (لأن) لنذكر سبب هذا الشعور. انتبه: felt هو الماضي غير المنتظم للفعل feel.
examples: I felt excited because I rode a camel.
My brother felt tired because we walked a lot.
We felt cold because the desert was windy at night.

words.ex: Can I have this blue T-shirt, please?
I like this bag. How much is it?
What size are these shoes?
This shirt is small. Do you have a bigger one?
Can I try on these trainers?
We paid the cashier and left the shop.

dialogue.t: Hello! Can I help you?
Yes, please. Can I have these red trainers?
Of course. What size are you?
Size 34. Can I try them on?
Sure. How are they?
They're too small. Do you have a bigger one?
Yes, here's size 35.
Perfect, thank you! How much are they?

grammar.title: Polite requests and comparatives (bigger / smaller)
grammar.ar: عند الشراء نطلب بأدب باستخدام Can I have ...? ونضيف please في النهاية. نسأل عن السعر بـ How much is it? للشيء الواحد و How much are they? للجمع. وللمقارنة نضيف er للصفة القصيرة مثل big ← bigger و small ← smaller، ونقول a bigger one بدل تكرار اسم الشيء.
examples: Can I have a smaller one, please?
How much are these socks?
Do you have a cheaper bag?

words.ex: On Eid we usually go to the Eid prayer early in the morning.
Children always wear new clothes on Eid.
We visit our relatives on the first day of Eid.
My mum makes delicious sweets for Eid.
My uncle always gives me Eidiya.
We celebrate Eid with our whole family.

dialogue.t: What do you do on Eid?
On Eid we usually wake up early and go to the Eid prayer.
Do you wear new clothes?
Yes, I always wear new clothes. Then we visit our relatives.
What does your grandmother do?
My grandmother always makes maamoul. It's my favourite!
Do you get Eidiya?
Yes! My uncles usually give us money and we buy toys.

grammar.title: Present Simple with always / usually / sometimes
grammar.ar: نستخدم المضارع البسيط للحديث عن العادات والتقاليد التي تتكرر. نضع كلمات التكرار مثل always (دائمًا) و usually (عادةً) و sometimes (أحيانًا) قبل الفعل. مع he و she و it نضيف s للفعل، مثل My grandmother always makes sweets.
examples: On Eid we usually visit my grandparents.
My dad always gives us Eidiya.
We sometimes go to the park in the evening.

words.ex: One day my cat jumped into the washing basket.
Suddenly the lights went off.
Then everybody started to laugh.
In the end we found the ball under the car.
My brother slipped on a banana skin.
We laughed and laughed all the way home.

dialogue.t: Let's make a funny story. One day a boy went to the park with his dog.
Suddenly the dog saw a cat and ran after it!
Then the boy ran after the dog and fell into the fountain.
Ha ha! He was all wet. Then a duck sat on his head!
Everybody in the park laughed.
In the end the dog came back with the boy's shoe.
That's a really funny story!

grammar.title: Time words to tell a story
grammar.ar: نستخدم كلمات الوقت لترتيب أحداث القصة بشكل واضح. نبدأ القصة بـ One day، ونستخدم Suddenly لحدث مفاجئ، و Then لما حدث بعد ذلك، و In the end لنهاية القصة. نحكي القصة بالماضي البسيط.
examples: One day my sister made a cake.
Suddenly the cake fell on the floor.
In the end we ate ice cream instead.

words.ex: We are going to visit the science museum on Saturday.
Let's go to the swimming pool!
How about playing video games after lunch?
We are going to have a picnic in the park.
A trip to the beach? That's a good idea!
The cinema? I'm not sure. It's very expensive.

dialogue.t: What are we going to do this weekend?
Let's go to the beach on Friday!
I'm not sure. It's going to be very hot.
OK. How about going to the water park?
That's a good idea! And on Saturday let's have a picnic.
Great! I'm going to bring sandwiches and juice.
And I'm going to bring a ball. We can play football.
Perfect! It's going to be a fun weekend.

grammar.title: going to for plans; Let's and How about for suggestions
grammar.ar: نستخدم am/is/are + going to + الفعل للحديث عن خطط قررناها للمستقبل، مثل We are going to swim. ونستخدم Let's + الفعل لنقترح فكرة، مثل Let's play. ونستخدم How about + فعل ينتهي بـ ing لنقترح فكرة أخرى، مثل How about swimming?
examples: I'm going to visit my grandmother on Friday.
Let's watch a film tonight.
How about riding our bikes in the park?

words.ex: A cheetah can run very fast.
Lions and tigers are wild animals.
Crocodiles are very dangerous.
An elephant is heavier than a horse.
I think dolphins are very intelligent.
I think the peacock is the most beautiful bird.

dialogue.t: Which wild animal do you like best?
I like cheetahs. A cheetah is faster than a lion.
That's true, but a lion is stronger than a cheetah.
Which animal do you think is the most dangerous?
I think the crocodile is the most dangerous animal.
Really? I think snakes are more dangerous than crocodiles!
Maybe. And the elephant is the heaviest animal on land.
Yes, and I think it's the most intelligent, too.

grammar.title: Comparatives and Superlatives
grammar.ar: نستخدم صيغة المقارنة لمقارنة شيئين: نضيف er إلى الصفة القصيرة ثم than مثل faster than، ونضع more قبل الصفة الطويلة مثل more dangerous than. ونستخدم صيغة التفضيل عند مقارنة شيء بمجموعة كاملة: the fastest أو the most dangerous. انتبه: في العربية نقول «الأسرع» بكلمة واحدة، أما في الإنجليزية فلا بد من the قبل صيغة التفضيل. وبعض الصفات شاذة مثل good ← better ← the best.
examples: A cheetah is faster than a lion.
A snake is more dangerous than a rabbit.
I think the elephant is the most intelligent animal.

words.ex: I feed my cat every morning.
You should clean the cage every week.
My brother takes our dog for a walk after school.
We took our rabbit to the vet because it was sick.
Your pet needs fresh water every day.
I brush my cat's fur on Fridays.

dialogue.t: I've got a new kitten! What should I do?
You should feed it every day and give it fresh water.
Can I give it chocolate?
No! You must not give it chocolate. It's bad for cats.
OK. What else?
You should brush its fur and play with it.
And if it gets sick?
Then you must take it to the vet.

grammar.title: should / must / must not
grammar.ar: نستخدم should لإعطاء نصيحة بمعنى «ينبغي»، ونستخدم must للتعبير عن أمر ضروري بمعنى «يجب». أما must not فتعني «يجب ألّا» أو «ممنوع». يأتي بعدها الفعل في صيغته الأساسية دائمًا، بدون to وبدون s، حتى مع he وshe وit.
examples: You should feed your fish every day.
You must take your dog to the vet when it is sick.
You must not leave your pet alone for a long time.

words.ex: Camels live in the desert.
Monkeys and parrots live in the rainforest.
Whales live in the ocean.
A camel stores fat in its hump.
Giraffes eat leaves from tall trees.
Many animals eat plants and grass.

dialogue.t: Where do camels live?
Camels live in the desert. It's very hot and dry there.
What do they eat?
They eat desert plants. They can live without water for many days because they store fat in their humps.
Wow! And where do penguins live?
They live in very cold places near the sea. They eat fish.
Can penguins fly?
No, they can't, but they can swim very well because they have strong wings.

grammar.title: Present Simple for Facts + can + because
grammar.ar: نستخدم المضارع البسيط للحديث عن حقائق ثابتة مثل أماكن عيش الحيوانات وطعامها، ونضيف s إلى الفعل مع he وshe وit مثل A camel lives. ونستخدم can للتعبير عن القدرة، ويأتي بعدها الفعل الأساسي. ونستخدم because بمعنى «لأنّ» لنشرح السبب.
examples: Camels live in the desert.
Giraffes can eat leaves from tall trees because they have long necks.
A polar bear lives in the Arctic and eats fish.

words.ex: It is usually sunny in Riyadh.
The sky is cloudy today.
London is often rainy.
It was very windy yesterday.
In winter there is snow in Canada.
It is usually hot in summer.

dialogue.t: What's the weather like in Buraidah?
In Buraidah it is usually hot and sunny, but in winter it is cold at night.
My cousin lives in London. In London it is often cloudy and rainy.
Does it snow there?
Sometimes, in winter. It is colder than Buraidah.
Which place do you like more?
I like Buraidah because I love the sun!
Me too, but I want to see snow one day.

grammar.title: Adverbs of Frequency + but
grammar.ar: كلمات التكرار مثل always (دائمًا) وusually (عادةً) وoften (غالبًا) وsometimes (أحيانًا) وnever (أبدًا) تخبرنا كم مرة يحدث الشيء. تأتي هذه الكلمات بعد الفعل is، وقبل الأفعال الأخرى مثل rains وsnows. ونستخدم but بمعنى «لكن» لنربط بين جملتين مختلفتين.
examples: In Buraidah it is usually sunny, but in London it is often rainy.
It never snows in Jeddah.
It sometimes rains in winter, but it is always hot in summer.

words.ex: We recycle paper and bottles at school.
Please put your rubbish in the bin.
Our class planted trees in the park.
We shouldn't waste water.
Plastic bags are bad for sea animals.
Turn off the lights when you leave the room.

dialogue.t: How can we help our planet?
We should recycle paper and bottles.
Good idea. We shouldn't use plastic bags because they hurt sea animals.
That's right. And we shouldn't waste water.
Why not?
Because there isn't much water in the desert.
We should plant more trees, too.
Yes! Let's plant a tree at our school.

grammar.title: should / shouldn't + because
grammar.ar: نستخدم should لنقول إنّ شيئًا ما فكرة جيدة، ونستخدم shouldn't وهي اختصار should not لنقول إنّ شيئًا ما فكرة سيئة. يأتي بعدهما الفعل في صيغته الأساسية. ثم نضيف because لنشرح السبب ونجعل رأينا أقوى.
examples: We should recycle bottles because it helps the planet.
We shouldn't throw rubbish in the sea because fish can die.
We should turn off the lights because we need to save energy.

words.ex: The monkeys are next to the parrots.
The café is opposite the lion area.
The zebras are between the giraffes and the elephants.
The tigers have a big enclosure with trees.
Many visitors come to the zoo on Fridays.
The penguins swim in a cold pool.

dialogue.t: Let's design our dream zoo! Which animals would you choose?
I would choose lions, penguins and giraffes.
Where would you put the giraffes?
I would put the giraffes next to the zebras because they both live in Africa.
Good idea. I wouldn't put the lions near the zebras!
Ha ha, no! I'd put the lions opposite the café, so visitors can watch them.
And the penguins?
I'd give them a big cold pool because they love swimming.

grammar.title: would for Imaginary Plans
grammar.ar: نستخدم would مع الفعل الأساسي للحديث عن أشياء متخيَّلة وليست حقيقية، مثل خططنا لحديقة حيوان الأحلام، وتعني تقريبًا «سوف» أو «كنتُ سأ...». اختصارها مع الضمائر هو I'd وyou'd، والنفي wouldn't. ويمكننا استخدامها مع كلمات المكان مثل next to وopposite وbetween، ثم because لنشرح اختيارنا.
examples: I would put the monkeys next to the parrots because they both live in the rainforest.
I'd build a big pool for the dolphins.
I wouldn't put the snakes near the café because visitors would be scared.

words.ex: Can I see the menu, please?
The waiter brought our drinks quickly.
Are you ready to order?
I'd like a glass of orange juice, please.
We had ice cream for dessert.
Could we have the bill, please?

dialogue.t: Good evening! Are you ready to order?
Yes, please. I'd like chicken and rice, please.
Of course. Would you like something to drink?
Could I have a glass of orange juice, please?
Sure. Anything else?
Can I see the dessert menu, please?
Here you are.
Thank you very much!

grammar.title: Polite requests: I'd like / Could I have / Can I
grammar.ar: نستخدم I'd like (وهي اختصار I would like) لنطلب شيئًا بأدب، وهي ألطف من I want. ونستخدم Could I have ...? وCan I ...? لنطلب شيئًا على شكل سؤال، وCould أكثر تهذيبًا من Can. أضف كلمة please في نهاية الطلب لتكون مهذبًا.
examples: I'd like a cheese sandwich, please.
Could I have some water, please?
Can I see the menu, please?

words.ex: Apples are a healthy snack.
Eating chips every day is unhealthy.
I eat vegetables with my lunch.
Cola has a lot of sugar.
Oranges have lots of vitamins.
I agree. Fruit is good for you.

dialogue.t: I think chocolate is unhealthy because it has a lot of sugar.
I agree. But I think dates are healthy.
Why do you think that?
Because they give you energy and they're natural.
I think chips are OK. They're made from potatoes.
I don't agree because they have a lot of oil and salt.
What about carrots?
Carrots are very healthy because they have lots of vitamins.

grammar.title: Giving opinions with because
grammar.ar: نستخدم I think ... لنعبّر عن رأينا، ثم نستخدم because (لأنّ) لنذكر السبب. إذا وافقنا على رأي شخص آخر نقول I agree، وإذا لم نوافق نقول I don't agree because .... انتبه: نقول I don't agree وليس I am not agree.
examples: I think milk is healthy because it makes your bones strong.
I think pizza is unhealthy because it has a lot of cheese.
I don't agree because juice has a lot of sugar.

words.ex: First, wash the tomatoes.
Then cut the cucumber into small pieces.
Finally, mix everything together.
Put the salad in a big bowl.
Be careful with the knife!
This is my grandma's recipe for hummus.

dialogue.t: Let's make a fruit salad! What do we do first?
First, wash the apples and the strawberries.
OK. What's next?
Then cut the fruit into small pieces. Be careful with the knife!
Done! Do we need a bowl?
Yes. Put the fruit in a big bowl and add some honey.
And then?
Finally, mix everything with a spoon. Yummy!

grammar.title: Instructions: imperatives with First, Then, Finally
grammar.ar: لإعطاء التعليمات نستخدم صيغة الأمر، أي نبدأ الجملة بالفعل مباشرة بدون فاعل، مثل Wash وCut. نرتّب الخطوات بكلمات First (أولًا) وThen (ثم) وFinally (أخيرًا). لا نضع you قبل الفعل في التعليمات.
examples: First, wash your hands.
Then cut the bread and add some cheese.
Finally, mix the eggs and the milk.

words.ex: My sister is good at tennis.
I practise basketball every Saturday.
There are eleven players in a football team.
Omar scored a goal in the last minute!
I can swim, but I can't dive yet.
I can't ride a horse yet.

dialogue.t: What sports do you like?
I love football. I'm good at running fast.
Can you score goals?
Yes, I can. But I can't kick the ball very far yet.
How often do you practise?
I practise with my team three times a week. What about you?
I'm good at swimming. I can swim fast, but I can't dive yet.
Cool! Maybe you can teach me to swim.

grammar.title: good at / can / can't ... yet
grammar.ar: بعد good at نستخدم اسمًا أو فعلًا ينتهي بـ ing، مثل good at swimming. بعد can وcan't نستخدم الفعل في صيغته الأصلية بدون to وبدون s. نضع yet في آخر الجملة المنفية لنقول إننا لا نستطيع الآن ولكن سنستطيع في المستقبل.
examples: I'm good at playing tennis.
She can ride a bike, but she can't skate yet.
We can't play volleyball well yet.

words.ex: I have a headache because I didn't sleep well.
He ate too many sweets and now he has a stomachache.
You're very hot. You have a temperature.
My brother has a bad cough.
Take this medicine after breakfast.
You should stay at home and rest.

dialogue.t: Hello, come in and sit down. What's the matter?
I have a headache and a cough.
Do you have a temperature?
Yes, I think so. I feel very hot.
Let me see. You have a cold. You should stay in bed and rest.
Should I take some medicine?
Yes, take this medicine three times a day. And you should drink lots of water.
OK. Thank you, doctor.

grammar.title: Talking about illness and giving advice with should
grammar.ar: لوصف المرض نقول I have a ... مثل I have a headache، ولا نقول I am headache. نستخدم should (ينبغي أن) لتقديم نصيحة، وبعدها الفعل في صيغته الأصلية بدون to. للنفي نقول shouldn't.
examples: I have a stomachache.
You should go to bed early.
You shouldn't eat a lot of sweets.

words.ex: This is my plan for next week.
I'm going to eat fruit every day.
I eat pizza only once a week.
Nuts are a healthy snack.
I will go to bed early on school nights.
You should exercise for one hour every day.

dialogue.t: What's your healthy plan for next week?
I'm going to drink six glasses of water every day.
Good idea! What about sport?
On Monday I will play basketball, and on Friday I will go swimming with my dad.
Are you going to eat sweets?
Only once a week! I'm going to eat fruit as a healthy snack.
And when are you going to sleep?
I'm going to go to bed at nine o'clock every night.

grammar.title: Future plans: going to and will
grammar.ar: نستخدم be going to مع الفعل في صيغته الأصلية للحديث عن خطط قررناها من قبل، مثل I'm going to swim. ونستخدم will مع الفعل في صيغته الأصلية للحديث عن المستقبل أيضًا، ولا نضع to بعد will. نستخدم on مع أيام الأسبوع، مثل on Monday.
examples: I'm going to walk to school every day.
On Tuesday I will eat fish and vegetables.
We're going to play football on Saturday.
